newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W. Australia raises pool prices for barley, canola.
newsitem.headline: W. Australia raises pool prices for barley, canola.

text.p: The Grain Pool of Western Australia said it raised its 1997/98 pool indicator prices for malting barley and canola but held prices for feed barley and lupins steady.
The malting barley indicator price was raised by A$5.00 a tonne to A$195.00-A$205.00 a tonne, while the canola price was increased by A$3.00 a tonne to A$338.00-A$353.00 a tonne.
Steady feed barley and lupin indicator prices are A$152.00-A$157.00 and A$190.00-A$195.00 a tonne respectively.

Chief executive officer Kevin Swan said the changes for malting barley and canola reflected a likely decrease in production on Australia's east coast because of poor growing conditions associated with lack of rain.
"Yields are expected to be lower on the east coast this season, meaning reduced supply and so less competition for Western Australian grains," Swan said.
The Australian Canola Association recently reduced canola crop estimates for Australia by 100,000 tonnes to 694,000 tonnes, with the major shortfall expected to occur in the eastern states, he said.
